newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea arrests monk for security law violation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea arrests monk for security law violation.

text.p: South Korea's intelligence agency on Wednesday arrested one of the country's most prominent dissidents, a Buddhist monk, on charges of violating national security laws, agency officials said.

An official at the Agency for National Security Planning said that Park Yong-mo, 48, was alleged to have participated in the inauguration of an outlawed dissident group and had contacts with a Korean-Canadian harbouring pro-North Korean sympathies.
The official said Park had provided the Korean-Canadian with information on activities of dissident groups in the South since November 1994.

Park, better known in South Korea by his Buddhist name, Jin Gwan, was also accused of meeting two North Koreans during a trip to Beijing in September last year when he received $4,000 as expenses, the official said.
South Korea's national security law bans pro-communist activities and unauthorised contacts with the North.
The two Koreas have remained technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended with an armistice agreement.
